chapters.title: The money, the tours, the politics
chapters.dek: Who owns what, how pros get paid, and why there are two paddle rulebooks.

items.fact: Pros earn from four places: UPA contracts (guaranteed salary), prize money, MLP team contracts, and equipment deals (paddle, ball, apparel). The UPA says 2026 shifts pay from salary toward prize money.
The UPA's plan: up to $31M in player earnings starting 2026: $11M guaranteed, $15M domestic prize money (PPA + MLP), $5M international.
In the 2026 MLP draft the St. Louis Shock paid $1.23 million for Anna Bright and the New Jersey 5s paid $800,000 for Jorja Johnson. A salary cap and floor are expected for 2027.
Anna Leigh Waters left Paddletek for a long-term Franklin deal in January 2026. Terms weren't disclosed; the $10M figure going around is podcast speculation.
APP pro prize money: $1.5M across 2026, doubling to $3M in 2027 across 12 events.
The 2026 US Open in Naples drew more than 500 pros for a purse of more than $160,000.
UPA-A paddle certification costs a brand $10,000 a year plus $3,000 per paddle (valid 24 months), with paid rush options up to $7,500.
MLP and the PPA Tour merged in 2024 under the United Pickleball Association (UPA), which runs both.
In May 2024 the UPA replaced USA Pickleball as its governing body with its own UPA of America (UPA-A). USA Pickleball had been the only US governing body since 1984.

Two paddle rulebooks now: UPA-A certification (performance-tested: power and spin, after break-in) is required for PPA and MLP pro play since Sept 1, 2025. Amateur divisions just need the paddle on USA Pickleball's approved list.
UPA contracts are exclusive. In Dec 2025 it terminated three pros' contracts for playing unsanctioned events in Japan; they appealed.
USA Pickleball still sanctions the US Open in Naples and runs its own National Championships, and partners with the APP on Golden Ticket qualifiers.
The senior pro league (50+) formerly called the National Pickleball League is now Champions Series Pickleball, licensed since March 2026 as the MLP Champions Series, with 16 teams.

items.title: California Smash
items.body: Nine padded indoor courts, no membership required, daily open play and classes, and a bar and restaurant.

items.title: El Segundo Recreation Park
items.body: The city's team pickleball leagues: women's, mixed, men's and 4.5+, eight-week seasons. For other court use call 310-524-2700.

items.title: Holly Glen Park
items.body: Four hybrid tennis/pickleball courts. The city says bring your own net and equipment.

items.title: Betty Ainsworth Sports Center
items.body: Four hybrid courts where the city supplies nets and equipment. Easiest if you have no gear.

items.title: Manhattan Heights Park
items.body: Weekday 8am–noon drop-in with a monthly pass. Courts here and at Live Oak Park book online, 4 days ahead for residents, 3 for everyone else.

items.title: Alta Vista Park Racquet Center
items.body: Four lighted courts; $25 annual membership plus hourly fees, reservations up to 7 days ahead. Perry, Franklin, Anderson and Dale Page parks have shared first-come courts (bring a net).

items.title: Walteria Park

items.title: South Bay Tennis & Pickleball Center

chapters.title: Trips worth taking
chapters.dek: Places where the courts are the reason to go. Each has an official page and a ready Airbnb search for the town.

items.title: Naples, FL
items.body: Home of the US Open Pickleball Championships, ten years running. Next one: April 17–24, 2027.

items.title: San Diego, CA
items.body: 19 pickleball courts; hosts the USA Pickleball National Championships, Oct 31–Nov 8, 2026. Two hours down the 5.

items.title: Daytona Beach area, FL
items.body: A 49-court club open to visitors on a $15 day pass, with a free Pickleball 101 class.

items.title: Fort Lauderdale, FL
items.body: 43 courts (14 weatherproof) and what it calls the first pickleball stadium. Hosts the APP Tour Championships Dec 3–6.

items.title: Orange Beach, AL
items.body: New public complex (opened May 2026): 14 lighted courts, open 7am–10pm daily, plus 6 indoor courts nearby.

items.title: St. George, UT
items.body: 24 lighted outdoor courts; pickleball at the Huntsman World Senior Games every October. Zion is next door.

items.title: Los Barriles, Baja, Mexico
items.body: A pickleball resort: 10 courts, casitas and villas on site, open play most days ($20 day rate), Baja Classic tournament Nov 18–22, 2026.

items.title: Brisbane, Australia
items.body: PPA Tour Australia's Australian Pickleball Cup, Oct 13–18, 2026, at Pat Rafter Arena.

items.title: Greater Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
